title: Regulations to Ensure Safety for Migrant Workers Ferried in Lorries
what_it_is: Regulations to Ensure Safety for Migrant Workers Ferried in Lorries

sections.label: Migrant worker lorry transport questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about lorry accidents involving migrant workers, legality of carrying passengers, and reviewing safety regulations and costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how many accidents involving migrant workers transported in open lorries have occurred in the past five years; (b) how many of such accidents have been fatal; (c) whether it is legal to carry passengers in vehicles not intended for ferrying people and, if so, who takes responsibility when accidents happen; and (d) whether regulations can be improved to protect the safety of migrant workers during their daily commutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether LTA will review the safety regulations to enhance the level of safety of migrant workers being ferried in mini-lorries or to require that they be transported via buses.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether any study has been done to find out what are the estimated additional costs (as a percentage and in absolute quantum across the industry) as a result of regulations prohibiting the transport of workers in lorries and goods vehicles; (b) if yes, what are the findings of the study; and (c) what measures can be taken to assist with the increased costs associated with such a prohibition.

sections.label: Lorry injury rates 2019-2020
sections.summary: Injury rates for persons on board lorries were 8.1 per 1,000 in 2019 and 4.5 per 1,000 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2019, the injury rate of persons on-board lorries is about 8.1 per 1,000 lorries, which is lower than the injury rate of persons on-board all motor vehicles at 8.4 per 1,000 motor vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2020, traffic volumes were lower due to COVID-19 restrictions, and the injury rate of persons on-board lorries was about 4.5 per 1,000 lorries, compared to 5.6 persons on-board all motor vehicles per 1,000 motor vehicles.

sections.label: Road deaths on board lorries
sections.summary: An average of nine persons on board were killed yearly from 2011 to 2015, dropping to 2.6 yearly from 2016 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2015, an average of nine persons on-board per year were killed in road traffic accidents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: This dropped to 2.6 per year from 2016 to 2020, or 2.5 if we exclude 2020.

sections.label: Regulatory changes and industry pain
sections.summary: Regulatory changes now will cause more acute pain to the industry, which is severely affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Compared to 10 years ago, regulatory changes at this time will cause even more acute pain to the industry, given that the industry is being severely affected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Impact of further regulations
sections.summary: Further regulations will likely affect building projects, cause some companies to close, and lose workers' livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Further regulations will likely have impact on the completion of various building projects, from BTOs to MRTs to nursing homes and hospitals, spell the demise of some companies and the loss of workers' livelihoods.

sections.label: Government refining policies and regulations
sections.summary: The Government will continue refining policies and regulations to minimise such situations and reduce lorry accident rates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The Government will continue to refine our policies and regulations to further minimise such situations involving our workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have brought down the accident rates of lorries over the years and will continue to strive to do so.

sections.label: Reconvening workgroup on lorry safety
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry would reconvene a workgroup to re-study new proposals and vehicle design improvements over the last 11 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider, therefore, reconvening another workgroup to re-study new proposals as well as improvements in vehicle designs over the last 11 years that could potentially have new solutions to improve safety on board lorries?

sections.label: Foreign worker driving licence requirement
sections.summary: In 2015 foreign workers were required to pass a basic theory test and Class 3 driving licence, and a review of these measures is underway.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2015, they actually introduced the requirement of not just getting the foreign workers to take a basic theory test but also to pass our Class 3 driving licence if they want to drive the Class 3 vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And we are currently undertaking a review of the measures with the view of looking at how we can enhance these measures further, in order to improve safety for workers.

sections.label: Light goods vehicle speed limits
sections.summary: Light goods vehicles currently have a speed limit of 60 kilometres per hour or the posted vehicle speed, whichever is lower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Regarding speed limits, presently, such light goods vehicles already have a speed limit of either 60 kilometres per hour or the posted vehicle speed for that area, whichever is lower.

sections.label: Study on prohibiting worker transport
sections.summary: Estimating costs of prohibiting worker transport in lorries and goods vehicles requires understanding industry options and detailed study and consultation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Because on the ground, there are significant real practical and operational challenges on top of just cost considerations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But having said that, if we were to estimate the additional costs as a result of prohibiting the transport of workers in lorries and goods vehicles, then we will need to have an understanding of the options that the industry will pivot to, whether it is buses, minivans, goods-cum-passenger vehicles or even other options.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And we will need to, really, undertake the detailed study and consultation with the industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, it is something that we can consider as part of the review.
